title: Short Stuff: Nouns of assemblage... assemble!
summary: Josh and Chuck explore "nouns of assemblage" (also called terms of venery or collective nouns), tracing their popularity to the Book of St. Albans (1486) and the fifteenth-century fad for inventing them. They run through examples for birds, insects, pets and domestic animals, wild animals, and dogs, and note that many were meant as jokes or satire, such as a "gaggle" of women and geese, or a "parliament" of owls popularized by C. S. Lewis. The episode closes with a plug for the HowStuffWorks article on the topic.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to nouns of assemblage
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce nouns of assemblage, examples like a murder of crows and a harness of podcasters, and joke about band names and etymology.

segments.title: Book of St. Albans and the 1486 fad
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the Book of St. Albans (1486), a fifteenth-century guide to hunting, heraldry, and falconry, kicked off a craze for inventing collective nouns. They mention a chapter on beasts, fowls, and fish and note that many terms came from it.

segments.title: Terms of venery and the origins of the fad
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh explain that nouns of assemblage are also called terms of venery, that venery meant hunting, and that many terms were meant for animals, so human groups listed in the book were satire. The fad spread among younger people.

segments.title: Bird and insect collective nouns
segments.summary: The hosts list bird terms such as a murder of crows, an unkindness of ravens, a charm of finches, a college of cardinals, and a parliament of owls (popularized by C. S. Lewis), plus insect terms like a swarm of bees, a business of flies, and a flock of lice.

segments.title: Pet, domestic, wild, and dog collective nouns
segments.summary: Examples include a kindle of kittens, a pitle of puppies, a clouder of cats, a pride of lions, a wisdom of wombats, and dog terms such as a kennel, a cry, a mute, and a pack. A business of ferrets and a gam of whales are also mentioned.

segments.title: Wrap-up on collective nouns
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why some names fit, such as a prickle of hedgehogs and an obstinacy of buffalo, and joke about a spinoff podcast and Jeopardy.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck points listeners to the HowStuffWorks article on the topic, and the episode closes with production credits.
